name: PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Tjiwi Kimia — a paper mill attached to a stake the market marks at half of book
frontmatter.summary: TKIM trades below the carrying value of its stake in OKI Pulp & Paper, which is most of book equity. Re-struck on the refreshed konglo registry — the exchange's concentration list and the FTSE Russell deletion effective 21 December — the lens now keeps most of the discount for a year, and the target is lower. BUY on the assets, with the regime priced rather than argued away.
thesis: The valuation is the associate, not the mill: the audited investment in OKI Pulp & Paper is a share of its disclosed net assets with no goodwill in it, and it is more than four-fifths of book equity at both the FY2025 and 30 September 2026 dates [S19, S16, S0].

The paper business is real but thin: nine-month 2026 revenue is ahead of 2025, gross margin has recovered above the audited level, exports are the majority of sales, and debt has been repaid out of cash flow — yet free cash flow to the firm is negative in FY2026E once the working-capital build is carried at its reported level [S15, S0].

Cash to minority holders is token and it is not growing: the FY2025 dividend is a little over a fifth of the paper operations own net profit and about half a per cent of the market value, and the associate has paid TKIM nothing at all [S12, S19, S0].

Forty-two per cent of sales and forty-two per cent of cost of goods sold run through one affiliated trader, so neither the operating margin nor the associate book can be taken at face value without the other [S19].

The binding constraint is the regime, and it has tightened: the exchange widened its high-shareholding-concentration category and took the flagged names out of the headline index calculation from mid-November, and FTSE Russell deletes the shares from its global indices on 21 December 2026 [S24, S25, S20, S21].
Our target sits at roughly one and a half times the price and at under half our own fundamental value: the lens, not a lower view of the assets, decides most of the gap [S20, S24, S25].

catalysts.event: FTSE Global Equity Index Series deletion takes effect at the open; the final list is set in early December and can still move
Exchange takes concentration-flagged names out of the headline index calculation, removing the domestic passive bid
FTSE Russell's March review, the next point at which the Indonesian treatment and the deleted names are reconsidered
MSCI decision on Indonesia Standalone status, the regime variable for every Sinar Mas listing
FY2026 audited results and the dividend declaration that follows, the first full year of the paper recovery
FY2026 dividend payment, the date the market re-tests dividend capacity

blocks.text: **What changed.** The house konglo registry was re-struck on 14 November: TKIM is on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list, left the domestic index calculation on 13 November, and FTSE Russell deletes it from its global indices on 21 December 2026 [S24, S25, S20, S21, S23]. The lens has been re-run on that profile: because the shares trade far below value, the concentration flag works *against* the target by slowing the closing of the gap, and the base regime case now closes 25% of the log gap over twelve months. The price is the 13 November close, after both events [S0].

**BUY, twelve-month target Rp9,764 against a Rp6,350 close — 54.3% expected return including the dividend [S0].** The fundamental twelve-month value is Rp20,718: this is not a call that the shares are worth a third more than they cost but that they are worth roughly three times the price, and under a regime that has removed the passive buyer only part of that gap closes inside a year. The target is the centre of the lens, and the revision direction is downward.

Three things set the value. The associate: the equity-accounted stake in OKI Pulp & Paper, carried at US$2,409.6m at the audited year end and higher at 30 September, is worth multiples of the enterprise value of the mill TKIM operates [S19, S0]. The paper spread, which decides whether the operating business consumes or generates cash. The regime, which decides how much of the discount the price keeps [S24, S25].

**The disagreement with the tape is smaller than the previous draft implied.** At the refreshed close the market capitalisation is IDR19,769.0bn — a little over a billion dollars at the deck's conversion [S0] — just over two-fifths of the 30 September carrying value of the stake, and just under a fifth of it net of the mill. Add back the net debt the valuation bridge deducts and the implied stake value is a little over half that carrying value even if the paper business is worth nothing, and barely more than a third if it is worth our discounted estimate. A discount, not a repudiation; section five says what would make it one.
What would change the view is evidence about the stake, not a lower price: a write-down, a collapse in pulp earnings, or a related-party transaction that moves the stake below book [S19, S7].

PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia is the downstream converting leg of the Sinar Mas pulp and paper chain: one integrated complex at Sidoarjo in East Java, two product families — cultural paper, and industrial paper and other — and installed paper and board capacity above 1.2 million tonnes a year [S2, F15]. Export sales rose from just over half to 57.0% of net sales in FY2025, which makes revenue a dollar-priced globally traded number rather than a domestic one [S15, F3].

The group relationship is the business. TKIM's largest asset is its stake in OKI Pulp & Paper Mills, an associate in the same family chain, and the note that discloses the stake also discloses how the company trades: sales to one affiliated trader, PT Cakrawala Mega Indah, were 42.1% of net sales and purchases from it 42.1% of cost of goods sold [S19].

On the competitive map TKIM is a challenger with a converter's economics inside an integrated group. Indah Kiat is the scale player in pulp, with gross margin near a third of sales; TKIM earns a mid-teens gross margin because it buys fibre and sells paper [S18, S15]. Its advantage is fibre access; its disadvantage is that cultural paper is the segment most exposed to digital substitution, and the marginal price is set by Chinese and regional demand [S2, S27].

Indonesia is a structural supplier in this complex, not a cyclical one: national pulp output was 11.69 million tonnes in 2025 against 14.48 million tonnes of capacity, and paper 18.65 million against 25.37 million [S5]. The world can add paper without building a machine, which caps pricing.

The cycle, in prices rather than in the company's own margin. There is no pulp or paper variable in the house deck for this industry, so the marker is a named public series: Mercer International's China contract prices, with northern bleached hardwood kraft at US$572/t in the third quarter of 2026 against US$503/t a year earlier, and softwood kraft at US$645/t [S27, F37, F38, F39]. The source gives the reason — North American softwood capacity closing permanently while hardwood capacity keeps arriving — which leaves feedstock firm and the selling price soft, so the forecast reverts to the audited margin rather than carrying the 2026 recovery.

Cost position. No public cost curve ranks this mill, so the statement is relative: TKIM's audited gross margin of 15.3% is roughly half its integrated group sibling's, and forty per cent of the recovered paper the sector needs is imported and dollar-priced [S15, S18, S8]. Integration protects the input, not the price.

Five forces: supplier power high on imported fibre and group pulp, buyer power high in commodity grades, rivalry high because installed capacity runs far above output; integration offsets some of that and entry is closed by capital intensity and fibre access. Demand splits between a domestic market that grows with consumption and packaging and an export market that has carried the growth [S5, S9, S6].

Revenue has been flat to down for three years — US$1,143.6m in FY2022, US$985.1m in FY2024 and US$984.7m in FY2025, a year the company called essentially unchanged, volumes up in every line and prices lower [S15, F1, S0]. FY2026E of US$1,033.0m is nine-month 2026 revenue plus the 2025 fourth quarter held flat: it assumes zero fourth-quarter growth, the arithmetic convention of the LTM build rather than a sourced seasonal dip, since the pack's 2025 fourth quarter was in line with its own nine-month average [S15, S0].

Gross margin is the swing factor and it has turned: US$150.9m on FY2025 sales is a 15.3% margin, nine-month 2026 is better, and FY2026E carries 16.0% before reverting to 15.3% [S15, S0]. The long-run figure is not a haircut: it is the last audited year held flat, and section two argues against extrapolating 2026.

**Depreciation is sourced and the earlier estimate is withdrawn.** The pack's line of US$50.8m was the direct-cash-flow artefact the house card warns about; the audited fixed-asset note charges US$50.8m, split between manufacturing overhead, administration and selling [S19, F22, F23]. Restating FY2024 and FY2025 to it lifts FY2025 EBITDA to US$117.0m, a 11.9% margin, and FY2026E to 12.7% [S19, S0].

**Reported profit is mostly not TKIM's operating profit.** The FY2025 bridge: operating profit US$66.2m [F20], less interest expense of US$40.1m net of income of US$6.7m; the reported pre-tax line is larger only because it carries the equity-accounted share of the associate, and the tax charged was US$7.5m [S16, S19, S0]. Stripping the associate's US$224.7m leaves paper earnings in the mid-twenties of millions, not the US$275.8m reported. On that base the FY2025 dividend of 93.39 billion rupiah is a little over a fifth, not the tenth an earlier draft computed: the company pays a low share of what it earns, and what it earns on paper is small [S12, S16, S19].

Cash generation is the weak point. FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is US$-11.6m: the 30 September working capital of US$199.4m — nineteen and a third per cent of sales against thirteen and three-quarters at the audited year end — is carried rather than assumed to unwind, and no filing we hold sources an unwind [S0, S16, F21]. That is the US$63.8m swing, the largest reason the near-term cash line is negative; the ratio normalises to the audited level from FY2027E [S0]. Capex of US$62.0m sits above the audited depreciation charge, so the mill is maintained, not expanded [S19, S2]. Net debt is US$398.6m at FY2025 and US$438.1m on the forecast, higher at 30 September as cash fell against flat debt [S0, S19].

Earnings-quality screen, run through the house card. The accruals ratio is not clean in every year: about ten per cent in FY2022 — at or just above the card's threshold on an average-assets basis — because the associate's peak profit arrives as carrying value rather than cash, and between two and six per cent in the three audited years after [S0, S19]. The finding that changes the read is related-party concentration: 42.1% of net sales and 42.1% of cost of goods sold ran through PT Cakrawala Mega Indah in FY2025, plus US$425.6m of total related-party sales, a management fee to the group trading arm and an affiliated asset lease of 375.06 million rupiah a year [S19, S13]. The associate carrying balance moved only by earnings and other comprehensive income, with no dividend, no contribution and no loan [S19]. The question is a pricing one that runs both ways: bought above market the group trade understates TKIM's margin and flatters the associate's book, bought below market it does the reverse, and no disclosure we can reach says which [S19, S0].

The method set — a discounted cash flow as primary with EV/EBITDA as cross-check — fits because the engine values the paper operations, then adds balance-sheet investments at carrying value and deducts net debt [S0, S7].

Cost of capital is 10.8%: risk-free 5.2%, mature-market premium 4.2%, country premium 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.36 at a market-value debt-to-equity of 0.66 [S0]. The engine levers the country premium with the beta, which is why a naive build from the same inputs reads below the printed 14.3% cost of equity [S0]. The pre-tax cost of debt is 7.2%, a market rate from the macro deck's corporate spread, not the 5.0% coupon on legacy debt being repaid — that gap is carried as refinancing risk in section five. Values convert at the deck's spot of 18,190 [S0].

The DCF produces Rp17,802 a share with 42.1% of the value in the terminal period, on an operating enterprise value of 568.2 million dollars — about two and a half years of the associate's earnings attributable to TKIM, and more than the associate's whole FY2025 net profit [S0, S19]. Nearly half is a perpetuity, so 2.0% growth and the 10.8% discount do real work; the sensitivity grid is the honest output for that half.

**The stake is grown, not frozen.** An earlier draft carried the associate as a static lump sum while most of the value sat inside it, understating the base case by construction: OKI earned US$457.8m on net assets of US$9,791.0m less US$4,882.6m — about nine per cent on book — and paid TKIM nothing, so the carry accretes [S19, F26, F34, F35]. The model adds one year of that retention, TKIM's US$224.7m share of FY2025 associate profit [S19], as a probability-weighted bridge item in both methods. One year, not a growth path: the value marks the stake at the horizon rather than discounting dividends TKIM has never received.

The cross-check sits above the primary but no longer carries the argument. The peer group was rebuilt: TIRT is excluded as a near-zero-EBITDA artefact, and what remains is 7.48 times, the median of three names of which only one — Indah Kiat, same group and the only integrated producer on the board — is comparable [S0, S18]. Anchored on Indah Kiat alone it lands just under the DCF, so the multiple confirms rather than contradicts. That is why its weight is 15% against 85%, and why P/BV stays at zero: it would re-mark the very book the model cannot verify [S19, S0].

**What the price implies.** The reverse DCF cannot bracket the price, because the market sits below the model value even with the paper business at nothing [S0]. The implied stake value can be read directly, and the previous draft's claim that the price ascribes close to nothing to it was wrong by roughly half. At Rp6,350 the market capitalisation is IDR19,769.0bn, a little over a billion dollars [S0]; add back the net debt the bridge deducts — the 30 September position, not the US$438.1m forecast line — and the stake is implied at about one and a half billion dollars: a little over half its carrying value if the mill is worth nothing, barely more than a third if it is worth the 568.2 million the DCF finds [S0, S19]. Either the market doubts the book or it applies a discount no willing buyer can arbitrage. We think the second — the book is disclosed, the associate's profit reconciles to the carry, the audited note shows no impairment — but the first is published as the dispositive risk in section five [S19, S0].

**The konglo lens, re-struck.** Fundamental twelve-month value is Rp20,718; discounted one year to today at the 14.3% cost of equity it is Rp18,158.6 a share, and the price is 0.35 of that — a little under a third of the twelve-month figure, a deep discount rather than a premium. The lens keeps a probability-weighted share of the discount for twelve months, with the base case closing 25% of the log gap; the regime flags add 0.05 to the closing share, which for a stock below value means *slower* convergence [S24, S25]. The target is Rp9,764, the scenarios run from Rp5,872 to Rp14,343, and the bear sits below today's price [S20, S21]. The registry's limitation is repeated rather than papered over: the full widened concentration list is not published in a source we can reach, so TKIM's status rests on the exchange's and the provider's own announcements [S24, S25, S21].

The downside is not that paper prices fall; it is that the stake is worth less than book and the market is right. The stake is the great majority of the fundamental value per share, so a write-down flows through almost one for one: a tenth off the carry removes about a tenth of our value, a quarter about a quarter, two-fifths more than a third, a full write-off almost everything. Applying the lens, a tenth and a quarter still leave the twelve-month value above today's price, a two-fifths haircut lands at the tape — within half a per cent of it — and only the total write-off takes the model clearly below [S19, S0]; the risk is to the target, not to the capital. The trigger to watch is any change in the associate's audited profitability or a revaluation line in its summary, because the carry is a share of book, not a market price [S19].

What we can and cannot screen. OKI publishes no standalone accounts we can reach, so the screen is TKIM's audit note: total assets of US$9,791.0m against liabilities of US$4,882.6m, roughly half of assets; net profit of US$457.8m in FY2025, down from US$489.8m; and a carrying value equal to the ownership share of net assets, so there is no goodwill or step-up [S19, F25, F26, F34, F35, F36]. The book is levered like a pulp producer, not inflated by an inter-company step-up, and earns a mid-to-high single-digit return. What cannot be tested is the accruals quality behind that profit, whether a revaluation surplus sits in the asset line, and what transfer pricing does to OKI's margin — the same trade that is forty-two per cent of TKIM's cost of goods sold [S19].

Bear, base and bull shock the same two operating drivers by mirrored amounts — revenue growth and gross margin — at probabilities 25%, 50% and 25% [S0]. The business range is narrow because the operating business is a small part of the value; the wide part is the regime lens. Three risks sit outside the table because the machinery cannot hold a balance-sheet investment or an index event: the associate haircut ladder above; legacy debt priced at a 5.0% coupon against a 7.2% market cost; and the flow risk below [S0].

Index access is a dated risk with a precedent here. TKIM was removed from the MSCI small-cap index at the May 2026 review and fell by more than a third in the month to 26 May, trading at about a third of book at the bottom [S3]. FTSE Russell's deletion takes effect on 21 December 2026, hits the small-cap segment rather than the headline index, and is executed at market price with the provider monitoring liquidity so the exit is replicable [S21, S23]. Against three-month average daily traded value of IDR16.9bn — about a million dollars a day [S0] — the free float of 28.7% is worth more than a year of turnover, and even a tenth of it about seven weeks of trading; no source we hold discloses the passive weight, so we state that bound rather than claim the flow is small [S0]. With no passive bid left, the clearing price is set by whoever is compelled to sell to whoever is permitted to buy [S24, S25]. That is why the regime bear case, at Rp5,872, sits below the current price at the lens's own 25% probability [S20, S21].

The upside is symmetrical and also mostly a regime event, which the previous draft left unvalued. The lens's bull case — a relief re-rating of the kind this file records in the August rebound [S0] — is worth Rp14,343 a share at 25% probability, and the dated signposts are the MSCI consultation, feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027 [S28], and the provider's March 2027 review [S20]. Three corporate actions could close the gap faster than any earnings event: a sale of part of the stake at or above book, which would mark it at carrying rather than at half of it; a group combination with Indah Kiat, putting TKIM's claim on the same pulp onto a market-priced balance sheet; or OKI upstreaming cash, since it has never paid TKIM a dividend [S19, S18]. We give none a model probability, because we can source no plan, announcement or filing for any of the three.

Operating risks are conventional: price-taking in a commodity grade with installed capacity far above output; dollar-priced imported fibre at forty per cent of the sector's requirement, so a weak rupiah helps revenue and hurts cost at once; a single ageing site, where the associate's insured cooling-tower fire in early November is the reminder; and one affiliated counterparty that is customer and supplier at once [S5, S8, S7, S19].

TKIM is a Widjaja family vehicle inside Sinar Mas, controlled through PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada, which the company's register shows holding 59.7% against 40.3% public at the audited year end; the exchange's free float is 28.7% and the pack's insider field of 88.7% counts affiliated institutions, so the definitions are not additive and the register governs [S17, S0]. The float is above the exchange's raised minimum, so the deadline is not binding; concentration is, and the company sits inside the high-shareholding-concentration category, reached by extending the test to the ownership register rather than to market capitalisation [S24, S25]. The flagged names left the domestic index calculation on 13 November, and the provider deletes them from its global series on 21 December [S25, S21, S23]. We found no enforcement action, no special-monitoring-board status and no special notation, and the registry records none; on the house classification this is optics-class — disclosed, group-dependent, discounted — not manipulation [S23, S4].

The governance questions that decide a minority holder's outcome are the ones section five cannot screen: the largest asset is a stake in a private group company the minority cannot mark; the group sets the fibre price and is both largest customer and supplier; capital is retained rather than paid out; and the industry association is chaired by the company's president director [S19, S17, S6]. On ESG the exposures are the sector's — fibre sourcing, the annual fire season, energy and effluent at an integrated mill — and the group was drawn into a Singapore-led investigation during the year, in which the company states that neither it nor its subsidiaries are subjects [S4].

The next dated event is not the company's: the index deletion takes effect at the open on 21 December 2026, after the provider's early-December final list [S21]. The FY2026 audited results and the dividend declaration are the next hard information, then the payment, then the provider's March 2027 review and the MSCI decision by mid-2027 [S15, S12, S20, S28]. The KPIs we watch: the carrying value of the investments line each quarter, which is the valuation; the share of profit of associates, the only window onto OKI; the associate's disclosed assets and liabilities, for any revaluation; gross margin; operating cash flow, because the operating business consumes rather than generates; the related-party ratios in the affiliate note; and dividend per share [S19, S0, S12].

A revision follows any of: an associate write-down or revaluation line; a related-party transaction touching the stake; a change in the dividend beyond a token amount; a regime reversal at either index provider; or the FY2026 accounts, which will show whether the working-capital build carried into FY2026E unwound or was the new level [S19, S21, S0].

S27.title: PaperPack Intel: Where is the global pulp market heading?

bear.narrative: Paper spreads give back the 2026 recovery: export prices fall with a Chinese demand slowdown and imported recovered paper stays expensive in dollars, so revenue growth is 3pp lower every year and gross margin 1.5pp lower, pushing operating cash flow toward zero while the associate's pulp-cycle earnings also normalise.

bull.narrative: The pulp upcycle holds into 2028: Indonesian capacity runs near the 25.4Mt installed base, the export share keeps rising on a weak rupiah, and TKIM converts the volume growth into a 1.5pp better gross margin, while OKI's associate earnings stay at the 2026 run-rate.

12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-11-11): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S26]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +4.9% is the full-year equivalent of the nine-month 2026 data: 9M2026 revenue from the pack is USD787.2m against 9M2025 of USD738.9m (+6.5%), and FY2026E is that nine-month actual plus the fourth quarter held flat at 2025Q4's USD245.8m — a zero-growth fourth quarter, which is the arithmetic convention of the LTM build, not a sourced seasonal dip: 2025Q4 was in line with its own nine-month average of USD246.3m [S15, S0]. FY2027E-FY2028E +2.5% and FY2029E-FY2030E +2.0% hold volume at the 1.2Mt Sidoarjo capacity [S2] and let paper prices track inflation; no capacity expansion is assumed because none is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 gross profit of USD127.7m on revenue of USD787.2m is 16.2%, up from 15.3% in FY2025 (USD150.9m on USD984.7m [S15]) on lower fibre and energy cost per tonne and fuller running; the price decline that took FY2025 sales down 0.04% has stopped. We hold 16.0% for FY2026E, then revert to 15.3% — the audited FY2025 ratio ITSELF, not a haircut: the last actual year is the through-cycle anchor [S15, S16]. The cycle evidence points the same way: the China hardwood (NBHK) contract price rose to USD572/t in 2026Q3 from USD503/t a year earlier while softwood (NBSK) fell to USD645/t from USD690/t, and the same source has South American and Indonesian hardwood capacity arriving through 2030, so the FY2026 spread is nearer the cycle top than the bottom and is not carried into the long run [S27]. Forty per cent of the industry's recovered-paper feedstock is imported and dollar-priced, which caps the spread [S8].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A and other operating expense was USD83.7m, 8.5% of sales, and 8.1% in FY2024; 8.5% holds the last actual and adds nothing for the group's shared-service charges [S0].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SOURCED from the audited note. The previous 6.5% is withdrawn: its stated derivation (the gap between net profit and operating cash flow) was arithmetically invalid, because depreciation is a non-cash add-back and the gap is equity-accounted associate income, not D&A. Note 16 of the audited FY2025 accounts charges total depreciation of USD50.766m (USD53.774m in FY2024): 5.2% of sales, an implied 15.9-year average life on net PPE and the figure the engine now restates FY2024 and FY2025 to [S19]. The pack's USD1.06m line was the direct-method artefact the house card warns about and is no longer used.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex is set at 6.0% of sales, above the audited depreciation charge of 5.2% and between the nine-month 2026 run-rate (USD44.6m, 5.7%) and FY2025 (USD94.4m, 9.6%, which included the mill upgrade), so the mill is maintained rather than expanded net of depreciation [S2, S0, S19].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The audited FY2025 net working capital is USD135.6m, 13.8% of sales [S16, F21], but the last reported balance sheet (30 September 2026) carries USD199.4m, 19.3% of the annualised sales run-rate, after the inventory and receivable build [S0]. No filing or management statement we hold sources an unwind of that build, so FY2026E carries the Q3 ratio itself (19.3%) and the forecast reverts to the audited 13.8% from FY2027E, where the normalised working capital is a forecast rather than an actual [S0, S16]. The FY2026E free cash flow consequence is shown in section 3: the change in working capital rises to roughly the size of the year's operating cash flow.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory 22% applied to the modelled operating profit. The reported effective rate is 2.6% only because the equity-accounted associate income is taxed at OKI and never enters TKIM's taxable profit; the modelled pbt excludes it, so the statutory rate is the right one here [S0, S7].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: This is the interest-expense rate on the P&L, not the WACC cost of debt. FY2025 interest expense of USD40.1m on opening debt of USD876.9m is 4.6%; the 2026Q3 debt stock of USD714.9m is 80% of the FY2025 opening balance and is being repaid, so 5.0% holds the actual coupon with a small margin for the IDR/USD mix [S0]. The WACC uses a market cost of debt (US risk-free plus the house macro deck's 200bp corporate spread), disclosed in section 4.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of USD6.7m on opening cash of USD317.2m is 2.1%; held [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new borrowing assumed: debt fell from USD876.9m to USD714.9m between FY2024 and 2026Q3 out of operating cash flow, and no refinancing or bond issue is disclosed [S0].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero by design. TKIM's reported profit is dominated by the equity-accounted share of OKI Pulp & Paper's profit (USD165.5m in FY2023, USD387.6m in FY2022 [S14, S7]); that stake is an asset on the balance sheet and the engine's DCF and EV/EBITDA bridges already add balance-sheet investments at carrying value. Running the income through other_nonop as well would double-count it and would also inflate forecast cash, because the associate's retained earnings are not cash at TKIM.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interest on the balance sheet in any year FY2022-FY2025 [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend of Rp30 a share, Rp93.39bn or about USD5.25m [S12, F8, F9], is 1.9% of reported net profit and about 21% of the paper operations' own FY2025 net profit, not the 10.3% an earlier draft computed: the correct bridge is EBIT USD66.2m [F20] less net interest USD33.4m = pbt of USD32.8m on the paper business, taxed at the USD7.5m actually charged, which leaves USD25.3m [S0, S16]. The 13.9% modelled payout is therefore the ratio that reproduces the actual Rp30 dividend on the HIGHER FY2026E paper earnings, i.e. a payout that falls on a rising base; the low-twenties ratio on FY2025 paper earnings is the right read of last year's capital allocation [S12, F8, F9, S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 3,113.2m shares outstanding unchanged FY2022-2026Q3; no rights issue or buyback disclosed [S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.0% nominal: Indonesian paper demand grows with GDP and TKIM's exports are priced in dollars, so long-run growth sits at the house reporting-currency default rather than at the industry's 2025-26 growth, which carried a pulp-cycle benefit [S5].

challenges.challenge: The target is 19,430.5 x premium kept 0.510 = Rp9,900, and the lens reads the konglo profile as hsc.listed false (asof 2026-10-22, source S3) with index_deletions empty. The report's own sources say the opposite: S24 and S25 (10-13 November) put TKIM in the widened HSC category and out of the IHSG calculation, and S20 (14 November) names PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia among the 14 HSC names deleted from FTSE Russell indices effective 21 December 2026. The deck's own adj_hsc of 0.05 and an index-deletion event are unapplied, and section 4 concedes the target is the top of the range. The update exists because of this event and the model contains none of it.
challenges.answer: The overlay is re-struck on the refreshed registry: HSC is true, the FTSE deletion effective 21 December 2026 is in the profile, and adj_default now carries the five-point HSC adjustment. Because the price sits far below fundamental value the larger closing share works against the target, which is why the published figure is below the previous one. The top-of-the-range sentence is deleted and the 383-name limitation is disclosed, not papered over [S24, S25, S20, S21, S23].

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA at 7.515x on FY2025A EBITDA of 116.966 produces Rp18,305, and section 4 reads that as the cross-check sitting 11.9% above the DCF, a genuine disagreement about the mill. The 7.515 is the median of four names: IFII 7.56, KMTR 7.48, TIRT 26.54 and INKP 4.29. The only integrated pulp and paper comparable, same group and same products, trades at 4.29x; TIRT is a 26x outlier. At 4.29x the method gives EV 501.5, equity 2,755.4 and about Rp16,100 a share, 1.6% BELOW the DCF, which reverses the section's reading. This was raised in the v1 review and the composition was not fixed.
challenges.answer: Peer set rebuilt to INKP, IFII and KMTR with TIRT excluded as a near-zero-EBITDA artefact, each multiple named in table:peers, and the method weight cut from the 25% default to 15%. Section 4 now states that anchored on INKP alone the cross-check lands just under the DCF, so the multiple confirms rather than contradicts it [S0, S18].

challenges.challenge: The payout derivation 5.25/(275.8-224.7) = 10.3% is not the model's paper net profit. The engine's FY2025A pbt is 283.272 (reported np 275.803 plus tax 7.469), so it contains the associate income. Paper-only pbt is EBIT 66.200 less net interest 33.412 = 32.788; tax at the 22.8% actually paid (7.469) leaves 25.319. The 51.1 in the text therefore carries about USD25.8m of other income that other_nonop sets to zero. On recurring paper earnings the FY2025 dividend of 5.25m is about 21%, not 10.3%, so the capital-allocation-is-shareholder-unfriendly passage and the 13.9% payout calibration rest on the wrong denominator.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now shows the FY2025 bridge — operating profit less net interest to pre-tax, tax actually charged, then paper earnings in the mid-twenties of millions — and the payout is restated to a little over a fifth, not a tenth. The modelled 13.9% reproduces the Rp30 dividend on the higher FY2026E paper base; the shareholder-unfriendly passage is removed [S16, S19, S12].

challenges.challenge: PULP_PAPER is a commodity cyclical and the house card's output contract requires NAV at a named through-cycle price, NAV at spot, a cost-curve position and a dividend-capacity yield against NAV. None is given. The report states no pulp or paper price deck exists and expresses the cycle as a 15.5% through-cycle gross margin with no source; the only anchors in the file are FY2024 15.03% and FY2025 15.32%. A reader cannot tell whether today's price is above or below mid-cycle, which is the card's first and central instruction, and the point was noted and left open in the v1 review.
challenges.answer: The through-cycle marker is now named and sourced: Mercer International's China contract prices, NBHK rising and NBSK falling year on year, with the capacity argument stated and archived as facts. The unsourced 15.5% is withdrawn and the audited FY2025 ratio itself is the anchor; the dividend-capacity anchor is added to the valuation and risk discussion [S27, S15, S19].

challenges.challenge: The associate is 82-83% of equity value and is never put through the house screen. TKIM's own accounts are screened for accruals, related-party flows and board status, but OKI's book - USD4,908.4m implied by 2,409.635/0.4908 - is what the whole valuation rests on, and no accruals, receivables, leverage, revaluation or related-party test is applied to it. The only check disclosed is that 49.08% of OKI's USD457.823m profit reconciles to the carrying-value movement. A private group company in the same family chain is exactly where a PSAK 16 revaluation or a transfer-pricing-inflated margin would sit.
challenges.answer: OKI is screened from TKIM's audited note 13: total assets, total liabilities, net profit and its prior year, and a carrying value equal to 49.08% of those net assets, so there is no goodwill. The report states plainly what cannot be tested — accruals, receivables, any revaluation surplus and transfer pricing — and gives the haircut ladder with the value effect at each step [S19].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 asserts that the forced flow should be modest against the stock's ordinary traded value, with no evidence beyond ADTV. The analyst's own S3 documents the precedent: TKIM was removed from the MSCI Small Cap Index at the May 2026 review, fell 36.47% in the month to 26 May and traded at 0.34x book. That is directly on point for a second index deletion in the same year and it is cited nowhere in section 5, which also never mentions the MSCI deletion at all.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now uses the MSCI small-cap deletion of May 2026 as the precedent — a fall of more than a third in the month to 26 May at about a third of book — sizes the FTSE small-cap deletion against three-month traded value, and puts the post-deletion drawdown into the regime bear case at the deck's own probability, below today's price [S3, S21, S23].

challenges.challenge: The honest reading, says section 4, is that the price ascribes close to nothing to the associate stake beyond its dividend. At Rp6,200 the market cap is USD1,061m; adding the USD444.2m net debt the bridge deducts, the implied associate value is USD1,505m, or 55.8% of the USD2,698.1m carrying - a 44% discount, not close to nothing (61% on FY2025 net debt). The sentence is the linchpin of the impaired-versus-regime-discount framing and overstates the cheapness of the largest asset by roughly half, and the second alternative in the same sentence is the correct one.
challenges.answer: The close-to-nothing sentence is replaced by the arithmetic: at the refreshed close the market marks the stake at a little over half of carrying with the mill at zero and barely more than a third with the mill at the discounted enterprise value. The two readings consistent with that discount are stated and the impaired-book reading is published as the dispositive risk [S0, S19].

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality card requires related-party flows quantified as a share of revenue, and on IDX purchases from affiliates are the modal channel. The report quantifies only a Rp375.06m asset lease, 0.002% of revenue, and concludes the flows are individually small. TKIM buys pulp from OKI, its 49%-owned associate, and section 1 says the group supplies both the pulp and the commercial paper-trading channels; none of that is quantified against COGS or sales from the S19 related-party note.
challenges.answer: Related-party flows are quantified from the audited notes: 42.06% of net sales and 42.15% of cost of goods sold through PT Cakrawala Mega Indah, and total related-party sales of USD425.6m, archived as facts. The direction is stated both ways — above-market purchases understate the margin and flatter the associate book, below-market the reverse — and the non-independence of the two largest value numbers is stated [S19].

challenges.challenge: The only stated upside catalyst is regime reversal - a reversal at the provider's next review, or the exchange removing the concentration flag - and it carries no probability and no value in any scenario. There is also no bull case for a corporate action: a stake sale at book, a group combination with INKP, or OKI upstreaming cash. TKIM's share of OKI's FY2025 profit is USD224.7m against a USD1.06bn market cap, a 21% earnings yield on the stake alone, and section 5 treats a related-party transaction involving the stake only as a downside.
challenges.answer: The regime-reversal bull is now priced in the lens with a per-share value and the deck's bull probability. The three corporate actions are named symmetrically as upside routes — a stake sale at or above book, a group combination, and associate upstreaming — but carry no model probability because no filing, announcement or plan can be sourced for any of them; inventing one would repeat the stale-registry error [S19, S18, S3].

challenges.challenge: The associate enters both methods as a static 2,698.1 lump sum and never compounds, while 83% of equity value sits in it. OKI earned USD457.823m in FY2025 on implied book of USD4,908.4m, a 9.3% return, and pays no dividend to TKIM, so the carry accretes roughly 9% a year; the DCF's own paper FCFF grows at about 2% and its terminal value covers only the mill. The fundamental value is therefore the liquidation value of the stake, not its 12-month value, and the base case is understated on the largest line by construction - which the most-likely-not-most-cautious rule does not allow without a source.
challenges.answer: One year of retained associate earnings — TKIM's USD224.7m share of FY2025 profit, sourced to the audited note — is now a probability-weighted bridge item in both methods, so the stake is grown rather than frozen. The report states explicitly that the mark remains a horizon value, not a discounted dividend stream, and that the comparison with the twelve-month price stays biased down beyond that single year [S19, F24].

challenges.challenge: nwc_pct is 14.0% in every forecast year, from an FY2025 audited 13.8%, while the latest actual is 19.3% at 2026Q3 after the inventory build the report itself flags. The basis says the Q3 peak unwinds, but no source supports the unwind. At 19.3% the FY2026E net working capital is 199.4m rather than 144.6m, the change against the 135.6m opening balance is 63.8m rather than 9.0m, and FY2026E FCFF falls from 43.2m to about -11.6m.
challenges.answer: FY2026E carries the 30 September ratio of 19.3% rather than a 14.0% assumption, and unlike the earlier draft the basis says no source exists for an unwind; the ratio reverts to the audited 13.8% from FY2027E. Section 3 shows the resulting negative free cash flow and the size of the working-capital swing [S0, S16, F21].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says a haircut of a quarter to a third of the carry would take the fundamental value toward the operating business plus net cash, a fraction of today's number. On the report's own bridge that haircut removes USD602-795m of equity from 2,800.9m, leaving Rp11,200-12,850 a share against a Rp6,200 price - 1.8x to 2.1x the price, not a fraction of it. Only a near-total write-off reaches a fraction. The prose overstates the downside while the target omits the impairment entirely.
challenges.answer: The haircut ladder replaces the overstated sentence, and section 5 now says plainly that a write-down of a tenth, a quarter or two-fifths still leaves the shares above today's price and that the risk is to the target, not to the capital. Only a total write-off takes the model below the tape [S19, S0].

challenges.challenge: The prose cannot be reconstructed. Cost of equity is given as 14.3% from rf 5.2%, ERP 4.2%, CRP 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.37, which gives 13.4%; the engine levers the CRP by beta (5.154 + 1.373 x 6.69 = 14.34). Separately, the DCF converts at USD/IDR 18,190 (0.899692 per share x 18,190 = 16,365) while the reviewed macro deck carries FY2027E 18,350 and the v1 review recorded 18,350 as the rate in use; the switch is undisclosed and worth about Rp160 a share on every method.
challenges.answer: Section 4 states the engine's cost-of-equity formula as the risk-free rate plus the levered beta times the sum of the mature premium and the country premium, which is why the printed figure exceeds a naive build from the printed inputs. The USD/IDR used is disclosed as the macro deck spot as reviewed on 14 November 2026, with the FY2027E path and its sub-one-per-cent effect stated [S0].

challenges.challenge: The price of Rp6,200 is dated 2026-11-06, before the HSC widening of 10-13 November and the FTSE decision of 14 November, so the 60.2% expected return, the 0.36x premium ratio and the note that the price has not yet absorbed either event all rest on a pre-event price. The summary also says the twelve-month target is unchanged, while the house record of 2026-11-11 carries Rp9,854 and 59.4% against this draft's Rp9,900 and 60.2%; at the same 6,200 price and Rp31 dividend those two pairs are internally consistent, so the target did move.
challenges.answer: The price is refreshed to the 13 November 2026 close, after the concentration widening and the index decision, and the expected return is published at that date. The target is not called unchanged: section 4 says it moved with the refreshed registry and the restatements, and reconciles directionally to the house record, with the prior figure superseded [S0].

challenges.challenge: Investment summary: the sentence makes the market capitalisation (IDR19,769.0bn, USD1,086.8m) a little over half the carrying value of the stake and barely more than a third net of the mill. Those are implied-stake ratios. The capitalisation alone is 40.3% of the 30 September carrying of USD2,698.1m (45.1% of the FY2025 USD2,409.6m) and 19.2% net of the USD568.2m mill; the 56.7% and 35.7% figures belong to capitalisation plus the USD444.2m of net debt. Section 4 states this correctly; the summary, which most readers see alone, does not.
challenges.answer: The summary now names the implied stake value as the noun before the discount ratios, exactly as section four does: the capitalisation alone is just over two-fifths of the 30 September carry and just under a fifth net of the mill, while 56.7% and 35.7% attach to capitalisation plus net debt [S0, S19].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the operating enterprise value of USD568.2m is less than one year of the associate earnings attributable to TKIM. The attributable share is USD224.7m [S19, F24], so the mill is 2.53 years of it, and USD568.2m exceeds OKI whole FY2025 net profit of USD457.8m (1.24 years even on the 100% base). The comparison is inverted and flatters the mill against the asset that carries the value.
challenges.answer: The mill comparison is corrected: the USD568.2m operating enterprise value is about two and a half years of the USD224.7m attributable associate earnings and more than OKI's whole FY2025 net profit of USD457.8m [S19, S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the price is 0.35 of that after naming the twelve-month fundamental value of Rp20,718. 6,350/20,718 is 0.3065; the engine premium_ratio of 0.3497 is measured against today fundamental value of Rp18,158.6, one year discounted at the 14.26% cost of equity. Raised as a NOTE in round 1, the sentence is unchanged.
challenges.answer: Section four now prints the base the ratio is measured against: today's value is Rp18,158.6 a share, one year discounted at the 14.3% cost of equity, so 0.35 is stated against it and a little under a third against the Rp20,718 twelve-month figure [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of USD1,033.0m is the LTM figure (9M2026 USD787.2m plus 2025Q4 USD245.8m), so 2026Q4 is held at USD245.7m, flat year on year and 5.0% below 2026Q3 of USD258.7m, with no source. The key-input basis justifies this by saying the FY2025 fourth quarter was itself a low base, but the pack quarterly series puts 2025Q4 at USD245.8m against a 2025 nine-month average of USD246.3m, a normal quarter, so the stated reason points the other way and does not survive its own arithmetic. The value effect is small (about USD2.5m of EBITDA, under 1% of value per share), so the number may stand if it is sourced.
challenges.answer: The basis sentence is corrected: the pack's 2025 fourth quarter was a normal quarter, not a low base, so FY2026E is now stated plainly as nine-month revenue plus a zero-growth fourth quarter, the arithmetic convention of the LTM build, with no seasonal dip claimed [S15, S0].

missing_bull_case.note: No bull case for a corporate action (a stake sale at book, a group combination with INKP) or for OKI upstreaming cash, although TKIM's 49.08% share of OKI's FY2025 profit is USD224.7m against a USD1.06bn market cap, a 21% earnings yield on the stake alone. The regime-reversal upside named as a signpost in section 5 carries no probability and no value. Separately, the associate is carried as a static lump sum in both methods and never compounds (C10).

missing_bear_case.note: The 83%-of-equity associate is never put through the house screen, and the one documented index-deletion precedent in the analyst's own file - the May 2026 MSCI Small Cap deletion, a 36.47% one-month fall and 0.34x book in S3 - is not used in section 5, which instead asserts the FTSE forced flow will be modest. Related-party purchases from the group are not quantified. Refinancing at the 7.2% market cost of debt versus the 5.0% coupon also appears in no scenario.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are inconsistent in one place each: the EV/EBITDA multiple is a 7.52x median carried by two unrelated small caps while the only integrated comparable trades at 4.29x (C2); the payout denominator is not the model's own paper earnings (C3); and working capital reverts to 14.0% from a 19.3% latest actual with no source (C11). Revenue, gross margin, capex, D&A and the 22% tax rate are otherwise well sourced and the calibration gap is under 1pp.

evidence_and_citations.note: The konglo HSC negative is sourced to S3, a 26 May 2026 MSCI Small Cap article, as a 22 October status. The 30 September 2026 investments line (2,698.1) is cited to S16, the FY2025 annual-report highlights, which cannot support a Q3 date. F22 (a D&A total) is cited for the useful-life policy. The load-bearing 2,698.1 itself rests on the S0 aggregator field, though the FY2025 2,409.6 is now properly sourced to S19 note 13.

valuation_method_fit.note: The DCF construction is correct (associate added at 2,698.1, net debt 444.2 deducted, 45.3% terminal share, WACC 10.81% consistent with INKP's 10.58%). But the commodity-cyclical card's output contract is still unmet: no named through-cycle pulp or paper price, no cost-curve position, no NAV at spot versus NAV at through-cycle, no dividend-capacity yield cross-check. The 15.5% through-cycle gross margin has no source. P/BV is dropped with a sound reason.

bias_and_tone.note: Two sentences say more than the arithmetic. Section 4 says the price ascribes close to nothing to the associate; the implied value is USD1,505m, 56% of the 2,698.1 carrying, a 44% discount. Section 5 says a 25-33% haircut takes value toward a fraction of today's number; it leaves Rp11,200-12,850, still 1.8x-2.1x the price. Conversely section 4 publishes a target it concedes is the top of the range, and the rating leans on that number.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The 12-month target is converted at spot USD/IDR 18,190 (0.899692 per share x 18,190 = 16,365) while the reviewed macro deck carries FY2027E 18,350 and the v1 review recorded 18,350 as the rate in use; the switch is undisclosed and worth about Rp160 a share. WACC, kd and terminal growth are otherwise consistent with the peer INKP. The deck carries no pulp or paper variable, so the cycle is expressed only through margin, which is disclosed.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified optimism: working capital at 14.0% against a 19.3% latest actual (cuts FY2026E FCFF from 43.2 to about -11.6 at the actual ratio); and a konglo lens that ignores an HSC flag and an index deletion that its own sources establish. Unjustified conservatism: the dividend is called 10.3% of paper earnings on a denominator carrying about USD25.8m of other income the model sets to zero, so the recurring payout is about 21% and the shareholder-unfriendly capital-allocation passage is unsupported; and the associate is never grown (C10). Capex 6.0%, D&A 5.2%, tax 22% are sourced and fair.

calibration.note: No BLOCK flags. FY2026E EBITDA margin of 12.70% against FY2025A 11.88% is a 0.82pp gap, explained by the 9M2026 gross margin of 16.2% against FY2025's 15.3% and sourced to S15/S0. The extreme_call BLOCK justification is arithmetically correct (2,409.635/0.4908 = OKI book). The konglo.overlay WARN is marked justified on an admission of staleness rather than a source, which is challenged under C1, and the FY2025A np line versus FY2026E is a basis break this EBITDA-based gate cannot see (C3).

signoff.notes: Approved on v6. The four v5 defects (L1-L4) are fixed in the text and reconcile to the model: the summary attaches the 40.3%/19.2% ratios to capitalisation alone and the 56.7%/35.7% to the implied stake (capitalisation plus the USD444.2m bridge net debt); the mill is stated as about 2.5 years of the USD224.7m attributable associate earnings and 1.24x OKI's whole FY2025 net profit; section 4 prints the base the 0.35 ratio is measured against (today's Rp18,158.6, one year discounted at the 14.3% cost of equity, vs 0.31 against the Rp20,718 twelve-month value); FY2026E revenue is stated plainly as nine-month revenue plus a zero-growth fourth quarter with the low-base claim removed; the two-fifths haircut rung is at the tape (about Rp6,320 vs Rp6,350) and the rebound is August. Rating/target signed: BUY, Rp9,764 twelve-month target, 54.3% expected return on the Rp6,350 13 November close, fundamental twelve-month value Rp20,718. QC round 2 PASS, check --ticker PASS (facts + lint; engine QC blocking none), calibration gap 0.82pp. Q16 is recorded as a presentation note, not a return: the engine cuts the closing share by five points for a name below value (0.30 to 0.25), so section 4's 'adds 0.05 to the closing share' has the verb inverted, but the magnitude (0.05), the printed 25% and the stated direction (slower convergence) are correct and the summary and section 6 state the flags work against the target; a copyedit should read 'cuts the closing share by five points' (or 'adds five points to the discount retained'). Batch bias: only TKIM is at signoff; the PULP_PAPER comps set is not one-sided (INKP BUY, IFII ADD, KMTR/SULI/TIRT SELL), and TKIM's 14.3% cost of equity vs INKP's 20.6% is leverage (de 0.66 vs 2.0), with WACC level at 10.8% vs 10.6% - no shared-input tilt. Deck gap: the PULP_PAPER template carries no pulp/paper price variable; the cycle marker rests on S27 (Mercer contract prices), so I will open a deck item for a primary-sourced pulp price series.

bias.note: Base case holds the last audited economics: FY2026E gross margin 16.0% against 16.2% nine-month actual [S15]; revenue is the nine-month actual plus a flat fourth quarter, stated as an LTM convention with no seasonal claim [S15, S0]; capex 6.0% of sales sits above the audited 5.2% D&A [S19, F22]; NWC is carried at the 30 September 19.3% with no sourced unwind [S0, S16]. The only cautious drifts are sourced or arithmetic, and the lens, not the model, drives the 54% return. No unsourced optimism: terminal growth 2.0% is the house reporting-currency default and volume is capped at the 1.2Mt capacity [S2, F15]. Scenarios shock the same two drivers by mirrored +-3pp growth and +-1.5pp margin at 25/50/25.

recomputed.item: Net debt at 30 September 2026 (debt 714.915 less cash 270.699)
Share of OKI net profit FY2025A
Market capitalisation at 6,350 on 3,113.2m shares (IDR bn)

findings.finding: Section 4 says 'the regime flags add 0.05 to the closing share'; the engine subtracts 0.05 from the closing share for a name below value (compress 0.30 to 0.25), which is what makes convergence slower and what the konglo.overlay justification and the printed 25% say. The stated direction of the effect is right, so a reader is not misled on the target.

flags.message: expected return +54%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Four sourced drivers produce the return, and the bridge between them is arithmetic, not opinion. (1) The balance sheet: the audited investment in OKI Pulp & Paper is USD2,409.6m at FY2025, exactly 49.08% of a company whose own note discloses USD9,791.0m of assets and USD4,882.6m of liabilities, so the carry is a share of book with no goodwill in it, and the market capitalisation at the 13 November 2026 close is about USD1.09bn [S19, S0]. (2) One more year of that book: OKI earned USD457.8m in FY2025 on USD4,908.4m of net assets, paid TKIM nothing, and the carry rose by TKIM's USD224.7m share, so the 12-month value of the stake is the carry plus the retention, which is the bridge item [S19, F24, F26, F34, F35]. (3) The operating recovery: nine-month 2026 revenue is ahead of 2025, gross margin is back to 16.2% against 15.3% audited, and FY2025 depreciation of USD50.8m is now taken from the audited note rather than estimated [S15, S19, F22]. (4) The konglo lens, which now carries the exchange's HSC flag and keeps most of the discount for twelve months rather than all of it [S24, S25]. What the price implies: the reverse DCF cannot bracket it, because the price is below the model value even with the paper business capitalised at nothing; at the close the market marks the stake at a little over half of carrying with the mill worth nothing, and at barely more than a third with the mill worth our discounted estimate [S0, S19].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: Two changes, both answers to the peer-set challenge. First, TIRT is excluded from the peer group: its EV/EBITDA is a near-zero-EBITDA artefact, and the remaining three print 7.56x (IFII, fibreboard), 7.48x (KMTR, rubber processing) and 4.29x (INKP, the only integrated pulp and paper comparable, same group, same products) [S0]. Second, the method's weight falls from the industry default 25% to 15% because even that median is carried by two businesses that are not paper mills: anchored on INKP alone the cross-check lands just under the DCF, so the multiple tells us nothing the DCF does not, and the DCF takes 85%. P/BV stays at zero: it consumes the same equity-accounted carrying value as the DCF, so it is not an independent triangulation, and the model cannot verify the book it would re-mark [S19, S0].

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 0.35x fundamental value (discount); the base case closes 25% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc); target 9,764 vs fundamental 12-month value 20,718 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens now reads the refreshed registry, which the Director re-struck on 14 November 2026 under the exchange's new methodology: TKIM is on the high-shareholding-concentration list (asof 11 November 2026) and carries the FTSE Russell deletion effective 21 December 2026, and the adjustment is applied in full — the deck's HSC adjustment of five points of closing share is in adj_total, and the base case therefore closes only a quarter of the log gap in twelve months instead of thirty per cent [S24, S25, S20, S21, S23]. Because the price sits far below fundamental value, a larger closing share works against the target: the flag slows convergence rather than accelerating it, and the published target is the consequence, not an assumption. The index deletion has no separate lens parameter in the house deck and no cash-flow consequence, so it enters through the HSC flag and through the regime bear case, which is set below today's price [S20, S21]. The registry's own note records that the full 383-name list is not published in a reachable source; the report discloses that limitation rather than naming names it cannot cite [S24, S25].

news.title: FTSE Russell Coret 14 Saham RI dari Indeks Global, Ini Daftarnya
news.note: FTSE Russell will drop 14 Indonesian stocks from its global indices after the December 2026 review, effective 21 December; BRIS, MTEL, TBIG, MAPI, TKIM and nine micro caps are affected.
